en.title: Consecutive Ones After Flipping at Most k Zeros
en.description:
Given a binary array, you may flip at most k 0s to 1s. Find the length of the longest run of consecutive 1s after the operation; you do not have to use all the flips.

The input format, examples, and test data were compiled and written by CSWork.
en.input: The first line contains n k (1≤n≤100000, 0≤k≤n); the second line contains n values, each 0 or 1.
en.output: Output the answer as described; separate multiple results with spaces in order, and output an empty line for an empty array.
en.explanation: Example 1: flipping the two 0s at indices 4 and 5 turns the range [4,9] into 6 consecutive 1s; there is no longer range containing only two 0s.
hints: Use a sliding window that tracks the number of zeros inside it; when it exceeds k, shrink from the left, and record the maximum length over all valid windows.
